newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telet responds to Brazil cell phone ruling.
newsitem.headline: Telet responds to Brazil cell phone ruling.

text.p: The Telet SA consortium on Monday insisted it was fully qualified to handle large mobile telephone concessions in Brazil.
The group made the claim in a statement responding to last week's high court ruling barring it from bidding on B Band licenses for Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro states.
"The total number of cellular telephone subscribers of Telet's three operators far exceeds the minimum 1.8 million required by the bid specifications," Telet said.
Telet's operating partners are BCE Inc's Bell Canada unit and Telesystem International Wireless Inc, and Malaysia's Technology Resources Industries Bhd, or TRI.

The statement said Telet "reiterates its full confidence in Brazil and in the Brazilian justice system," but it did not say if the group planned to appeal the ruling by Superior Justice Tribunal Judge Antonio de Padua Ribeiro.
Last week, a Telet spokesman said the group's lawyers would study the ruling before deciding whether to appeal.
Ribeiro ruled in the government's favor Friday by tossing out an injunction that allowed Telet to continue bidding for concessions even though it was disqualified by the Communications Ministry.
The statement Monday was the latest twist in an increasingly public dispute between Telet and Communications Minister Sergio Motta.
Motta ruled in June that Telet could not take part in bids for concessions to provide B Band cellular services in three regions that cover Sao Paulo city, Sao Paulo state and Rio de Janeiro state.

Telet then won an injunction that allowed it to continue in the bidding process, pending a future ruling on the merit of its appeal. Although a group including Bell South Corp. won the Sao Paulo city concession earlier this month, Telet remained in the running for the other two concessions.
Officials from the Telet group complained they were unfairly disqualifed by the minister even though a ministry committee approved its participation.
In a statement Friday, the court said Judge Ribeiro agreed with Motta's view that the consortium lacked technical experience to handle the three biggest B Band contracts.

On Monday, Telet said Bell Canada operates more than 10 million fixed lines and its subsidiaries in Canada, China, Colombia, India and other countries provide cellular service to 1.5 million subscribers.
Telesystem, Canada's largest private telecom, and its TIW unit provide cellular services in partnership with companies in Canada and other countries.
TRI owns Celcom, Malaysia's and Southeast Asia's largest cell phone operator, with 900,000 subscribers.
Telet remains in the running for three smaller concessions.
